title: Tenant-scoped audit sink contracts: retries, DLQs, signing, and observability
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Problem: Customers expect deterministic delivery behavior from audit exports (SIEM webhooks, Splunk HEC, Datadog, and generic HTTP sinks). Current behavior is best-effort: retries are ad hoc, ordering/duplication guarantees are unclear, and tenants cannot easily inspect delivery health. Goal: ship a tenant-scoped audit sink contract that defines delivery semantics, retries/backoff, DLQ behavior, payload signing/encryption options, and observability surface. The contract must be configurable per-tenant and per-sink, respect RBAC v2 admin controls, and integrate with SSO-managed orgs so only authorized admins can change sink settings.
acceptance_criteria: Audit sinks can be created and configured per-tenant with UI and API controls guarded by RBAC v2 roles.

Delivery follows a documented contract: at-least-once delivery with idempotency keys, transparent retry/backoff, and a tenant DLQ when the sink is continuously unavailable for a configurable window (default 6 hours).
Payloads are signed (HMAC) and optionally encrypted; signing key rotation supported without loss of delivery guarantees.
Operational metrics: per-tenant outgoing queue depth, retry rate, DLQ size, last-success timestamp, latency P50/P95, and per-sink error reasons exported to Console and alerting rules.
Integration tests simulate transient failures, permanent failures, high-throughput, and ordering-dependent events and must pass in staging.
Migration: existing sinks remain functional; new contract applied only after opt-in or tenant migration window with audit log entries.
decisions: Choose at-least-once delivery with client-visible idempotency keys rather than striving for strict exactly-once (too expensive across network sinks).
DLQ modeled as per-tenant time-windowed store in our object store with retention policy; provides replay APIs for customers.
Use HMAC-SHA256 signing for payloads with per-tenant signing keys stored in KMS; optional envelope encryption for regulated customers.
Retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter, capped at 1 minute between retries, escalation to DLQ after N consecutive failures or elapsed time threshold (configurable).
Ordering: best-effort preservation within a tenant via sequence watermarks; no global cross-tenant ordering guarantee.
tradeoffs: At-least-once simplifies guarantees but requires customers to handle duplicates; we provide idempotency metadata to reduce customer burden.
Per-tenant DLQs and replay APIs increase storage/operational burden but greatly improve debuggability compared to silent drops.
Signing adds CPU overhead and latency; optional for low-risk sinks, enforced for high-security tenants.
implementation_plan: 1) Add sink contract schema to control-plane PM store (fields: retry_window, max_attempts, dlq_window, signing_enabled, encryption_profile).
2) Extend admin Console and REST API to create/update per-tenant sinks; enforce RBAC v2 checks and SSO group membership for admin flows.
3) Implement delivery worker changes: idempotency key header, signed payload generation, retry engine with pluggable backoff policy, and DLQ writer.
4) Build DLQ storage and replay API with pagination and replays limited by tenant quota.
5) Instrument detailed metrics and traces; add pre-built dashboard panels and alert templates in Console.
6) End-to-end tests + canary rollout to 5% of tenants, then full rollout behind feature flag.
testing_plan: Unit tests for signing, key rotation, and idempotency header generation.
Integration tests against mock SIEM endpoints that simulate 500s, 429s, timeouts, and slow responses.
Chaos test: network partition between runtime and sink endpoints to validate DLQ and replay behavior.
Load test: 10k events/sec across mixed tenants to validate worker throughput and queueing behavior.
Security test: verify signing keys never leak; KMS ACL and audit logs verified for admin actions.
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal enabled for Redwood internal telemetry and SRE team only.
Beta: opt-in for external tenants with a migration guide and support runbook.
Canary: 5% tenants with feature flag and tight SLAs, monitor DLQ growth and retry rates for 72 hours.
General availability: automatic tenant migration after 30-day opt-in window unless tenant opts out.
monitoring_and_alerting: Per-tenant alert: DLQ size > threshold (default 1000 events) -> page SRE and notify tenant admins.
Delivery failure rate > 1% over 5m -> baseline alert for platform health.
Signing failures or KMS errors -> security SEV1 until resolved.
Latency regression: P95 outbound latency increase > 2x baseline -> performance investigation ticket automatically created.
